title: The core strategic question is why Layer 3 hasn't produced a national winner, and PlayBlue needs a confident answer

body.text: Genuine multi-brand curated sports retail has been attempted repeatedly in India — Planet Sports at scale, Sports Station still operating today, Foot Locker now entering — without yet producing a profitable national chain. That is either the opportunity nobody has closed out, or a warning that the model runs into structural headwinds here: FDI friction on multi-brand structures, Layer 2 players matching price without sacrificing curation credibility, or thin margins that don't support the staffing "expert guidance" requires. PlayBlue's pitch, and its Series A story, needs an explicit answer to "why hasn't this worked at scale in India yet," not just "why we're the ones who can do it."

title: Sizing has to move from top-down to bottom-up before the Series A

body.text: The $30B figure will not survive diligence — goods-only forecasts land near $10.7B, and no two sources agree. Meanwhile the government's own data shows sub-1% sport participation. The defensible story is bottom-up: households above an income threshold, within a catchment, at measured activity rates, plus 12.3M gym members growing 11% a year. That is checkable, it is smaller, and it is far more persuasive to an investor whose portfolio is analytics-weighted.

title: Site selection is now the highest-value decision in the business

body.text: Grade A/A+ mall vacancy nationally is just 5.7%/2.6% (Q1 2026) even as overall leasing volume has cooled from its 2025 high, rents are up 12–22% on target high streets, 75% of national leasing concentrated in PlayBlue's three cities, and Decathlon is adding 80 stores into the same squeeze. At 15,000 sq ft, PlayBlue needs the scarcest category of space. In that market, catchment quality determines store economics more than format does — and a wrong site cannot be corrected without writing off capex the profitability target cannot absorb.

title: Price is the weakest ground against Layer 2; premium specialism is the opening

body.text: Decathlon's local sourcing and full-margin capture, the ₹500 Cr manufacturing push, and Technosport's vertical integration all widen the cost gap against a wholesale-buying retailer. But value growth outpaces volume, and premium is the faster-growing tier. The winnable position is premium and specialist rather than value — and the unresolved question is which specific categories carry premium willingness-to-pay in India today. That is measurable, and currently unmeasured.

title: All four stated differentiators are untested, and they carry very different costs

body.text: Curation, expert guidance, community and 4-hour delivery are asserted as reasons to choose PlayBlue. None has been validated with Indian consumers. Each has a different cost structure: expert guidance is a permanent staffing line, 4-hour delivery is fulfilment capex, community is a data and programming investment. If expert guidance drives preference it justifies its cost; if it does not, that cost is unrecovered on every store, forever. Testing four assumptions costs a fraction of building all four.

title: Layer 2 challengers are the fastest-growing threat, and “why not vertical integration” needs a rehearsed answer

body.text: Technosport and BlissClub are growing faster than anyone in PlayBlue's stated competitive set, and they win by owning product and customer rather than curating. Technosport's 300-store plan also contests the same scarce retail space. Any Series A conversation will surface these names. Having a considered answer to "why not vertical integration" is worth more than another slide on curation.

title: Profitability and community pull in opposite directions, and the sequencing is undecided

body.text: Operational profitability before Series A rewards tight cost control. A 10M-member community requires sustained investment before it returns anything. Both are stated goals. The resolvable question is not which to choose but what to _build_ now versus what to _design_ now and build later — and the data architecture is the part that is very expensive to retrofit and relatively cheap to specify upfront.

title: The multi-brand FDI question should be closed before it compounds across three more stores

body.text: Decathlon's own reported push to be reclassified multi-brand confirms the restriction is live. PlayBlue's model is definitionally multi-brand, and its seed round carries a Japanese co-lead investor. This is a structuring question for PlayBlue's counsel, not something we can resolve — but it is cheaper to close now, before Mumbai and Delhi NCR add scale to whatever the current structure is.
